entry.title: Gray Garden: A Digital Garden Template

link.title: Gray Garden: A Digital Garden Template

entry.content:
A digital garden template where content is seeded, grown, and intertwined. It’s built using the static site generator Jekyll, with Obsidian integrated in the workflow. The sample content was developed by exploring the subject Information Theory.

  • Explore the website: Gray Garden

entry.title: Nexae: A Digital Document System
entry.content:
Nexae is a digital document system developed by taking new approaches to representational concepts for mapping and accessing the interconnective structure of documents. The video below provides insight into its development and a walkthrough the current implementation of the prototype.

  • Visit the weblog for the research project documentation: Forking the Docuverse: A Digital Document System Developed For Mapping and Accessing the Interconnective Structure of Documents Through Interaction
  • Thanks to Max van Duijn, Edwin van der Heide, and Rafael Wlodarski for project support.

entry.title: One Puzzle, Two Ways of Puzzling

link.title: One Puzzle, Two Ways of Puzzling

entry.content:
Framed as a live experiment within an exhibition, this project invited participants to solve two slightly different memory-based puzzles on two different devices, allowing them to directly experience how different forms of bodily engagement shape cognitive performance. The video below is a demonstration of the installation setup.

  • In collaboration with Peng Song.
  • Shown at the exhibition Science to Experience at Snellius Gebouw, Leiden, The Netherlands 2020. Hosted by V2_ Lab for the Unstable Media.

entry.title: Architext
entry.content:
A prototype text editor that generates a node-link diagram and a timeline according to the text input. Architext allows people to construct non-sequential text structures by applying a syntax based on Markdown. It was created for an experiment that involved testing to what extent constructing different visual renditions of content can facilitate text comprehension.

Using social contract theory as sample content, the video below demonstrates one way information can be organized in Architext.

  • In collaboration with Benjamin Turner.

entry.title: Manufacturinng Habits
entry.content:
An installation combining a robot creature, a touchscreen device, and an interface to reveal how psychological manipulation is achieved through design.

  • Shown at the exhibition Ya! Present at Dutch Design Week, Eindhoven, The Netherlands, 2018.
  • Thanks to Thomas Buxo and Agata Jaworska for concept development support, Sander de Jong for coding assistance, and John Berthelsen for technical advice.
